# Frozen Code data and checks inventory v1

Prepared before product source/runtime. authored.json contains the exact CP context, valid payload literals V01–V04, output tuples/spans, and malformed patches M01–M19 with exact errors. Every offset in a patch is Code-payload-relative, zero-based; overwrite retains total length. Default method is name `m` (UTF16 [109]), flags0, one Code attribute name index1. CP3 deliberately Class(0): the catch check consumes CP-kind only. CP6 is a second `Code` name slot, CP7 UTF16 [0,55296]. Authoring is independent of future Rust output. The JSON is data, not an executable oracle. Tests use the same frozen literal strings and patches directly, avoiding a JSON parser dependency. Storage symbols S=size_of::<Option<CodeBody>>, H=size_of::<ExceptionHandler>, A=size_of::<Attribute>; no assumed 32/64-bit layout. Future Rust expectations use exactly these size_of expressions, not observed output allocation/capacity. H is four u16 fields. No architecture claim has been validated in this stage.

## Prefix, malformed, disposition and precedence inventory

- Every prefix length0..12 V01, 0..45 V02, 0..26 V03, 0..19 V04, and genuine Code lengths0..46/0..44/0..22 -> Truncated under adequate budgets. Prefix does not adjust declared lengths/counts or replace the entire class. Append00 to each full payload -> Malformed("code trailing bytes"). Exact valid full bytes succeed.
- M01–M19 are literal patches. M18's third declared handler consumes old nested bytes, yielding start2/end2: range error before nested framing. M19 declares65535 exception entries; existing method+outer records2 plus65535 exceed hard65535 BEFORE entry reads: Limit("code records"), even though bytes are absent. All other cases have adequate limits.
- Empty methods -> success empty even with zero Limits; unsupported version wins first; bad CP length wins second. Versions45.0/.1/.2/.3,46.0,67.0/68.0/69.0 accepted;44.0/45.4/46.1/67.65535/68.65535/69.65535/70.0 rejected exactly UnsupportedVersion{major,minor}. CP length0/65536 -> code constant pool size; no whole CP scan.
- Ordinary flags0,0x0008,0xffff with exact <clinit> require Code. Ordinary m flags0x0100,0x0400,0x0500 -> None with no Code and unexpected Code with any present (even malformed) Code. Exact <clinit> at flags0x0100/0x0400/0x0500 still requires one Code. UTF16 `<clinit>suffix` with native flags is ordinary/None. `<init>` is ordinary for this framing rule. Other flag combinations/descriptors/special-method legality unverified.
- Concrete with no attrs or only unknown attrs -> missing Code. Native with unknown attrs -> None but all unknown attributes are budgeted/name-checked. [V01,V02,V03] methods plus native/abstract empties preserve exact order and None alignment, duplicate method records retained independently.
- Two Code names at same CP or distinct CP1/CP6 -> duplicate Code. Malformed first payload + second Code -> duplicate; forbidden method first recognized Code -> unexpected; Code followed by bad-name outer attr -> CP error before Code body parsing. Required with unknown bad CP name and no Code -> CP error before missing.
- Method name and outer/nested name index0 (including forged Utf8 at CP0), index65535/out-of-range, CP5Unusable -> constant index; CP3Class/CP4Integer -> UTF8 index. Nonzero catch points at Utf8/Integer/etc -> class index; Unusable/out-of-range -> constant index; catch0 never resolves CP0 (even forged wrong CP0). Simultaneously bad exception range+bad catch -> code exception range first.
- Nested name CP errors precede missing nested u32 length, because text lookup is first. M16 u32MAX nested length -> Truncated on normal32/64-bit targets, and usize conversion failure likewise Truncated on narrower hypothetical target. Extra nested count with absent bytes -> Truncated after precharged records/storage unless limit exhausted first.
- Forged huge attributes/methods vectors, aliased payloads, many long/equal-prefix unknown names, malformed counts at end-of-input, and every single-byte xor with fixed masks01/80/ff across V01–V04 are finite no-panic cases. Mutations need only controlled Result unless explicitly classified above; do not require all mutated data to fail. No recursion follows even nested name Code.
